passwordHash.safetyNote: Passwords and salts are processed only inside this browser (in a Web Worker) and are never sent to a server, so even production passwords never leave your device.

algorithmHints.argon2: Winner of the Password Hashing Competition and the current recommendation. Use Argon2id for new systems.
algorithmHints.bcrypt: The default in many frameworks. Passwords are limited to 72 bytes.
algorithmHints.scrypt: A memory-hard key derivation function that makes attacks with dedicated hardware expensive.
algorithmHints.pbkdf2: A key derivation function used where FIPS 140 compliance is required. Computed with the Web Crypto API.

passwordHash.saltHint: Normally use a random value of 16 bytes or more. To reproduce an existing hash, enter the same salt.

passwordHash.defaultsNote: Defaults follow the OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet. Larger values are more secure but take longer to compute.
passwordHash.noEncodedNote: scrypt and PBKDF2 have no common storage format, so store the hash together with its salt and parameters.

markdownEditor.sampleMarkdown:
# ClientKit Markdown Editor

**ClientKit** is a collection of safe tools that run entirely in your browser.

## Features

- Real-time preview
- GitHub Flavored Markdown support
- One-click conversion to `HTML`

## Sample

1. Table

| Feature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Secure | No data is ever sent to a server |
| Fast | Everything runs in your browser |

2. Task list

- [x] Write some Markdown
- [ ] Check the preview

> Blockquotes are supported too.

Take a look at [ClientKit](https://clientkit.dev/en).

jsonSchemaValidator.specNote: Supported specification: JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 (validated only when $schema is omitted or set to the value below). format is treated as an annotation and not validated.

envCompare.safetyNote: Your .env contents are never sent to a server or saved in browser storage. Values are hidden by default.
syntaxRules: KEY=value (an optional leading export is allowed). Keys start with a letter or _ and may contain letters, digits, _, ., and -.
An = inside the value is kept as part of the value (only the first = separates key and value).
Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored. Outside quotes, # preceded by whitespace starts an inline comment.
In quoted values (" ' `), # is part of the value, and values may span multiple lines.
Variable expansion such as ${VAR} and command execution are never performed. Lines that can't be parsed are listed as errors.
envCompare.emptyState: Enter .env contents on both sides to list missing, duplicate, and empty keys.

invalidReasons.trailingText: extra text after the closing quote

errors.load: Couldn't load the image. The file may be corrupted.

sqlInsertGenerator.identifierHint: Table and column names are wrapped in double quotes, keeping case and symbols as-is.

csvRules: Every value is written as a string (leading zeros are kept).
Single quotes (') inside strings become ''. Backslashes are written as-is (assumes standard_conforming_strings = on).
Empty cells are written as empty strings ('') by default. Check the option below to write NULL instead.
jsonRules: null becomes NULL, numbers are written as-is, true / false become TRUE / FALSE, and strings become '...'.
Single quotes (') inside strings become ''. Backslashes are written as-is (assumes standard_conforming_strings = on).
Nested objects and arrays are errors. Choose below how to handle rows where a key is missing.
sqlInsertGenerator.missingLabel: Rows where a key is missing
sqlInsertGenerator.outputPlaceholder: Enter data and a table name to see INSERT statements here.
sqlInsertGenerator.stats: {rows} rows · {nulls} NULLs · {quotes} values with escaped quotes

jsonErrors.jsonSyntax: The JSON has a syntax error: {message}
jsonErrors.jsonNotArray: The JSON must be an array of objects ([{...}, {...}]).

jsonErrors.jsonUnsafeNumber: The number at {path} is too large to handle exactly. Write it as a string ("...").

insertErrors.nulCharacter: PostgreSQL can't store the NUL character (\u0000): {where}
insertErrors.missingKey: {row} has no "{column}" key. Add the value or change how missing keys are handled.

chmodCalculator.safetyNote: Calculations happen in your browser. No real file permissions are read or changed.
chmodCalculator.scopeNote: Covers read, write, and execute for owner, group, and others (three octal digits). setuid, setgid, the sticky bit (fourth digit), and ACLs are not covered.

fileMeaning.write: Change the contents (deleting or renaming the file depends on write permission on the parent directory).
fileMeaning.execute: Run it as a program or script.

directoryMeaning.read: List the names of the files inside (ls).
directoryMeaning.write: Create, delete, and rename files inside (execute is also required).
directoryMeaning.execute: Enter the directory (cd) and access files inside. Without it, you can't open files even if you know their names.

errors.invalidChar: Contains invalid characters. Octal uses 0–7; symbolic uses r, w, x, or - in their fixed positions.
errors.invalidLength: Enter 3 octal digits or 9 symbolic characters.
errors.specialBits: setuid, setgid, and the sticky bit are not supported.

cidrCalculator.safetyNote: All calculations happen in your browser. Addresses are never sent anywhere and no network connection is made. IPv4 only.
cidrCalculator.cidrLabel: IPv4 address and prefix length (CIDR notation)
cidrCalculator.emptyState: Enter a CIDR block such as 192.168.10.0/24 to see the network range.
cidrCalculator.normalized: {input} includes host bits, so it's calculated as the network range {network}.
cidrCalculator.usable31: (/31 is for point-to-point links; both addresses are usable per RFC 3021)
cidrCalculator.countNote: Total addresses counts every address in the range. For prefixes of /30 or shorter, usable hosts excludes the network and broadcast addresses.
cidrCalculator.containsLabel: IPv4 addresses to check (one per line)

errors.octetRange: Each number must be between 0 and 255.
errors.leadingZero: Numbers with leading zeros (such as 010) aren't allowed because some systems read them as octal.
errors.missingPrefix: Add a prefix length such as /24.
errors.prefixRange: The prefix length must be between 0 and 32.

gitignoreTester.safetyNote: Nothing you enter is sent to a server. All checks run in your browser.
scopeNotes: Checks one .gitignore at the repository root against paths relative to the root. Nested .gitignore files, .git/info/exclude, and global settings (core.excludesFile) are not covered.
Paths are treated as untracked files. .gitignore doesn't apply to files that are already committed (tracked); use git rm --cached to stop tracking them.
End directory paths with / (e.g. dist/). Matching is case-sensitive. Character class names such as [[:alpha:]] are not supported.
gitignoreTester.pathsLabel: Paths to check (one per line, directories end with /)
gitignoreTester.emptyState: Enter paths to see whether each one is ignored and why.
gitignoreTester.invalidPath: Can't be read as a relative path (empty segments, . and .. are not allowed).
gitignoreTester.reasonMatched: Excluded by the last matching rule.
gitignoreTester.reasonNegated: The last matching rule is a negation (!), so it isn't excluded.
gitignoreTester.reasonParent: The parent directory {dir} is excluded, so everything inside is ignored too.
gitignoreTester.ineffectiveNegation: The negation rule on line {line} matches this path but has no effect because a parent directory is excluded. Exclude the directory's contents instead (e.g. dir/**) to re-include it.

i18nPlaceholderChecker.safetyNote: Your translation files are never sent to a server. All checks run in your browser, and your JSON is never modified.
syntaxNotes: Only simple named placeholders like {name} (letters, digits, and _) are supported. Order and repetition don't matter as long as the set of names matches.
Escaping follows ICU MessageFormat: text quoted with apostrophes, such as '{' or '{name}', is literal, and '' is a single apostrophe. Ordinary apostrophes such as in don't stay as they are.
ICU syntax such as {count, plural, ...} or {gender, select, ...} is not supported and is reported as unsupported rather than passed. Double braces such as {{name}} are reported as unparseable.
i18nPlaceholderChecker.emptyState: Enter the source and translation JSON to check keys and placeholders.
i18nPlaceholderChecker.notObject: Both JSON documents must have an object ({ ... }) at the top level.
i18nPlaceholderChecker.noIssues: No problems with keys or placeholders were found.
i18nPlaceholderChecker.nonStringDetail: The value is {type}, so placeholders weren't checked.
i18nPlaceholderChecker.sideDetail: Check the {side} value. Placeholders weren't compared.

jsonSchemaGenerator.safetyNote: Your JSON is never sent to a server. The schema is generated entirely in your browser.
notes: Generates a starting point in JSON Schema Draft 2020-12. Only type, properties, and array items are output.

A single sample can't tell which fields are required or which values are allowed, so constraints such as required, enum, format, and minimums, as well as additionalProperties, are not added. Add them as needed.
All array items are combined into one schema. Mixed types become several types (or anyOf), and empty arrays have no items because the item type can't be determined.
jsonSchemaGenerator.parseError: JSON syntax error at line {line}, column {column}: {message}
jsonSchemaGenerator.emptyState: Enter sample JSON to see the generated JSON Schema here.
jsonSchemaGenerator.verified: The original sample was validated against the generated schema and passes.
jsonSchemaGenerator.verifyFailed: The original sample doesn't pass the generated schema.

openapiCompat.safetyNote: Your API definitions are never sent to a server. Everything is compared in your browser, and external $ref targets are never fetched.
scopeNotes: Supports OpenAPI 3.0.x definitions in JSON or YAML. OpenAPI 3.1 and Swagger 2.0 are not checked.

Detects removed paths and HTTP methods; parameters, request bodies, and request properties that became required; type changes; and nullable changes. Paths that differ only in parameter names (/users/{id} → /users/{userId}) are treated as the same endpoint.

$ref within the same document is resolved. References to external files or URLs and schemas using allOf, oneOf, anyOf, or not are reported as unchecked. enum, format, removed response properties, and more are not checked, so no findings doesn't guarantee full compatibility.
openapiCompat.emptyState: Enter the OpenAPI definitions before and after the change to see changes that affect existing clients.
openapiCompat.libraryLoadError: Couldn't load the YAML parser. Please reload the page.
openapiCompat.fixInput: Fix the errors in the definitions.
openapiCompat.notObject: {side} must be an OpenAPI definition object.
openapiCompat.unsupportedVersion: {side} isn't OpenAPI 3.0.x (openapi / swagger: {version}), so it isn't checked.
openapiCompat.noFindings: No breaking changes were found in the areas checked. Some areas aren't checked, so this doesn't guarantee full compatibility.

reasons.pathRemoved: Existing clients calling this path will get errors such as 404.
reasons.methodRemoved: Existing clients calling this method will get errors such as 404 or 405.
reasons.paramAdded: Existing clients don't send this parameter, so their requests will be rejected.
reasons.paramRequired: Existing clients that skipped this optional parameter will have their requests rejected.
reasons.bodyRequired: Existing clients that don't send a body will have their requests rejected.
reasons.mediaTypeRemoved: Requests from existing clients using this media type will no longer be accepted.
reasons.propertyRequired: Existing clients that don't send this property will have their requests rejected.
reasons.typeChanged: The type changed from {before} to {after}, so it no longer matches the values existing clients send or expect.
reasons.nullableChanged: nullable changed from {before} to {after}. This affects clients sending null in requests, or clients not expecting null in responses.
reasons.externalRef: The external reference ({before}) isn't fetched, so this wasn't checked.
reasons.unresolvedRef: The reference ({before}) can't be resolved within the document, so this wasn't checked.
reasons.composition: A schema using allOf, oneOf, anyOf, or not changed, which isn't checked.

pgExplainViewer.safetyNote: Your plan is never sent to a server. Everything is analyzed in your browser, with no database connection or SQL execution.
pgExplainViewer.parseError: JSON syntax error at line {line}, column {column}: {message}. If you're pasting from psql, use the output of FORMAT JSON.
pgExplainViewer.noPlan: No plan (JSON containing "Plan") was found. Paste the output of EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, FORMAT JSON).
pgExplainViewer.emptyState: Paste the output of EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, FORMAT JSON) to see the plan as a tree.
pgExplainViewer.notAnalyzed: This plan was captured without ANALYZE, so there are no actual rows, loops, or times (shown as "—").
pgExplainViewer.slowestHeading: Nodes with the most self time
pgExplainViewer.misestimateHeading: Nodes with the largest row misestimates
pgExplainViewer.timeNote: Estimated rows, actual rows, and actual time are per loop, as PostgreSQL reports them. "Self" is an estimate: the total over all loops minus the children's time, not a simple sum. Parallel nodes (under Gather) are divided by the number of processes, and negative values caused by CTEs or InitPlans are shown as 0.

robotsTxtTester.safetyNote: Nothing you enter is sent to a server. All checks run in your browser, and no site is accessed and no robots.txt is fetched.
specNotes: Matching follows RFC 9309 (Robots Exclusion Protocol). The group is chosen by an exact, case-insensitive match on the product token, falling back to the * group if none matches. Groups for the same user agent are combined.

Rules are matched from the start of the URL path (including the query), and the longest match wins. When an Allow and a Disallow of the same length conflict, Allow wins. * matches any characters and a trailing $ marks the end of the URL.

Only crawling is checked. An allowed URL isn't guaranteed to appear in search results, and a disallowed URL may still be listed (without content) if other pages link to it. Use noindex to keep a page out of results.
robotsTxtTester.agentError: Enter a product token (letters, _ and - only, e.g. Googlebot or Bingbot) — the crawler name, not a full browser user-agent string.
robotsTxtTester.urlsLabel: URLs or paths to check (one per line)
robotsTxtTester.emptyState: Enter robots.txt contents and URLs to see whether each one may be crawled.
robotsTxtTester.noGroup: No group (including *) applies to this user agent.
robotsTxtTester.invalidUrl: Can't be read as an http(s) URL or a path starting with /.

reasons.noGroup: No group applies, so there are no restrictions.
reasons.noRule: No rule matches, so it's allowed.

robotsTxtTester.unsupportedHeading: Directives not used for matching (such as Crawl-delay; outside RFC 9309)
robotsTxtTester.orphanHeading: Rules before any User-agent line, which belong to no group
robotsTxtTester.invalidHeading: Lines that can't be parsed (not in "name: value" form)

semverRange.safetyNote: Checks run in your browser and never query the npm registry. Only the candidate versions you enter are checked.
semverRange.includePrerelease: Always include prereleases such as 1.0.0-beta (like npm's --include-prerelease)
semverRange.emptyState: Enter a version range and candidate versions to see which ones are in range.
semverRange.prereleaseExcluded: Prereleases are only included when the range has a comparator with a prerelease on the same major.minor.patch, so this is out of range.

rangeErrors.tag: This is a dist-tag such as latest or next. The version it points to is decided by the registry, so it can't be checked as a range.
rangeErrors.nonRegistry: This is a Git URL, tarball, local path, or npm: alias, not a version range, so it can't be checked.
rangeErrors.invalid: This can't be parsed as a version range. Check the operators and version format.

sourceMapResolver.safetyNote: Your source map and stack trace are never sent to a server. Everything is resolved in your browser, and external maps or source URLs are never fetched.
sourceMapResolver.scopeNote: Supports a single Source Map v3 (indexed maps with sections are not supported). Stack traces in Chrome/Edge (at fn (url:line:column)) and Firefox/Safari (fn@url:line:column) formats are recognized.
sourceMapResolver.fileHint: Only frames for {file} are resolved (the URL path and query are ignored when comparing).
sourceMapResolver.fileHintAll: The map has no file field, so every frame is resolved with this map.
sourceMapResolver.columnBaseLabel: Column numbering in the stack trace
sourceMapResolver.emptyState: Enter a source map and a stack trace to see the original source locations.
sourceMapResolver.summary: Resolved {mapped} of {total} frames with a location.
sourceMapResolver.noSourcesContent: The map has no sourcesContent, so the source code can't be shown (the location is still resolved).

frameStatus.noLocation: This line has no location (file:line:column) and is shown as is.
frameStatus.otherFile: This frame belongs to a different file than the one specified, so it wasn't resolved.
frameStatus.unmapped: The map has no matching position. Check the column numbering and that the map matches the file.

mapErrors.syntax: Source map JSON syntax error at line {line}, column {column}: {message}
mapErrors.notObject: The source map must be a JSON object.
mapErrors.version: The source map version isn't 3 (version: {version}). Only v3 is supported.
mapErrors.indexed: Indexed maps with sections aren't supported. Enter a single, non-sectioned map.
